Milton Hershey's story 👇

slides.title:
After 4 years as an
apprentice, he opens his
own *candy shop*.
slides.sub:
In Philadelphia, timed for the
Centennial Exposition (Hershey Co.,
Hershey Community Archives).

slides.title:
Philadelphia: bankrupt
in 1882. New York:
*closed in 1886*.
slides.sub:
In between, in Denver, he learns to
make caramels with fresh milk.
Remember that (Hershey Archives).

slides.title:
Broke, he sells caramels
from a *pushcart*. Then a
big order from England.
slides.sub:
To fill it, a bank cashier backs
his loan with his own signature
(Hershey Community Archives).

slides.title:
At the Chicago World's
Fair, he sees *German
chocolate machines*.
slides.sub:
He buys them and installs them
in his caramel factory
(Hershey Community Archives).

slides.title:
1900: he sells the caramel
business for *$1 million*.
He keeps the chocolate.
slides.sub:
Buyer: American Caramel Company.
That same year, the first
Hershey bar goes on sale.

slides.title: Nobody told Mr. Hershey how to make *milk chocolate*. He just found out the hard way.
